Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and the same as G1102; properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth):--new.
BiblicalUsage: Agnaphos means unfulled — new cloth, not yet shrunk or finished. Jesus uses it in the parable of the patch: no one puts a piece of new cloth on an old garment, for the patch tears away and makes the tear worse.
TheologicalSignificance: New cloth on an old garment is the Lord's own picture, and this word only names the patch — the parable teaches, not the adjective.
